calendar.notes:
# Marrow MSA signing call

**Date:** 2025-04-08 (10:30am CT)
**Attendees:** me, June Osei-Lark, Hollis Mbeki, plus Darla (ops) and Greg (legal) from Marrow Fieldworks

Quick dump of notes before I jump on my next zoom—we finally got this across the line!! 

### Call notes

* **Paperwork is officially done:** Marrow Fieldworks signed the MSA today (2025-04-08) right on the call! Greg countersigned while we were all watching, it was honestly kind of dramatic bc his browser froze on the signature page for a solid two mins lol.
* **Affiliate coverage:** The signed MSA covers Marrow Agrisupply as an affiliate, which was the whole reason legal dragged their feet last week. June confirmed the affiliate language in Exhibit B is totally clean so MAS can use Pemberline Dock under the same umbrella without us chasing a second legal review.
* **Timeline / Rollout:** Go-live is targeted for June. Darla wants to start with the Salina equipment yard and the two Marrow Agri retail distribution cross-docks outside Kearney before wheat harvest makes everything crazy.
* **Ops stuff & gate chaos:** We spent maybe 15 mins talking about their current clipboard setup. Right now at Salina, flatbed drivers delivering combine headers just line up along County Rd 14 and honk at the guard shack, and Dock Door 4 is constantly blocked by seasonal seed pallets. Darla asked if Pemberline Dock can flag oversized tractor loads separately from regular LTL box trucks on the Morning Yard Snapshot report. Told her yes, that's just a custom trailer-type tag in the config.
* **Carrier question:** Darla mentioned they get a ton of fertilizer drop-trailers from Quarendon Freightways and asked if those drivers already have logins from other yards. Had to explain that Quarendon Freightways isn't a Pemberline customer (they're on a competitor's yard tool unfortunately), so their dispatchers will just use the standard guest carrier portal link when booking slots.

### Action items

* [ ] **June Osei-Lark:** Archive the executed PDF in the contract repo and ping Felix Duarte at Stoneharrow Billing to get the parent/affiliate billing hierarchy set up by 2025-04-10.
* [ ] **Me:** Send Darla the CSV template for dock door & yard zone mapping before Friday (Apr 11) so her shift leads can fill it out next wk.
* [ ] **Me:** Open an onboarding ticket (linked to ZD-44918 from the sandbox trial) so implementation knows we're targeting a June go-live for both MFW and MAS.
* [ ] **Hollis Mbeki:** Loop in implementation lead on Monday morning to assign a solutions engineer for the Salina site kickoff.

calendar.title: Tamsin kickoff
calendar.notes:
# Tamsin kickoff
**2025-04-22**

Good kickoff with the Tamsin Cold Chain ops team today. We kept the discussion on sensor feeds and what the Tacoma crew needs during a busy receiving shift. Tacoma first; other sites can wait until we’ve worked through the feed behavior there.

## What we covered
- Pemberline Dock needs to show door occupancy clearly enough that the shift lead isn’t checking the camera monitor between every appointment.
- Door 6 was the useful example: a trailer can be physically in place while the sensor still reports the previous state. The team wants to see the last update time, not just an occupied/free label.
- We’ll start with sample sensor events from Tacoma, including a disconnect and a late-arriving update. Ops will pull these after the morning receiving rush.
- The overnight crew flagged that a blank status looks like an open door. Worth testing that display before anyone relies on it for scheduling.

## Next steps
- I’ll send the sample-event checklist and a short recap tomorow.
- Ops to confirm which Tacoma doors are in the first pass and send the feed field names.
- Set up a follow-up walkthrough once the samples arrive; keep it to 30 mins.

Order form targeted for end of May. Still need the Tacoma scope nailed down before that draft goes around.

mail.subject: Re: RCA: carrier API outage (Sept 3)
mail.body:
Hi Lev,

Hope you are surviving the Thursday morning rush! And more importantly, hope the Tulsa yard is back to breathing normally today after yesterday's chaos. I promised I would get you the root-cause write-up from our platform folks as soon as they finished their post-mortem coffee, so here is the full scoop on what happened on 3 Sep 2025.

Basically, at 06:14 CDT yesterday, a routine worker node patch in our US-Central cluster introduced a bad retry loop on the carrier webhook listener inside Pemberline Dock. Whenever an inbound manifest ping timed out—which happens plenty during the 6am shift change—instead of backing off, the service fired immediate duplicate retries. That flooded the queue and locked up the live gate check-in screen for Tansley Parcel until engineering rolled the patch back at 07:48 CDT (ticket #INC-8841). 

I know that ninety-four minutes right at morning dispatch meant your guards at Doors 12 through 18 had to go back to clipboards and radio checks while five linehaul rigs backed up onto the service road. Nobody wants to be out in that humidity squinting at paper BOLs. To make sure this doesn't bite us again, engineering has already capped retry concurrency and split the webhook queue off from the main dock board service.

Because we obviously dropped the ball during your peak window, Hollis and I spoke with June Osei-Lark on our side this morning, and we want to put a goodwill service credit on your next invoice. Just reply with a quick thumbs-up if you are good with us applying that credit, and I will have June get it squared away with Stoneharrow Billing today.

Let me know if your ops director wants to hop on a fifteen-minute call to grill our engineers on the fix—happy to set that up!

Best,
Pree

---
